paragraphs: ¹¹ Wickedness fills the city; violence and deceit never leave its streets. ¹² It was not an enemy who taunted me — I could have endured that. It was not a foe who rose against me — I could have hidden from him. ¹³ But it was you — someone like me, my companion, my close friend. ¹⁴ We used to share deep conversation and walk together to the house of God. ¹⁵ Let death take them by surprise; let them go down alive to the grave — for evil lives in their homes, in their very hearts.

¹⁶ As for me, I will call out to God, and the LORD will save me. ¹⁷ Evening, morning, and noon I pour out my anguish and cry aloud — and he hears my voice. ¹⁸ He rescues me in peace from the battle raging against me, though many oppose me. ¹⁹ God will hear and bring them low — he who has reigned from ancient times. Selah. For they refuse to change, and so they do not fear God. ²⁰ They turn on those who are at peace with them, breaking every promise they made.

²¹ His words were smoother than butter, yet war was in his heart. His speech was softer than oil, yet every word was a drawn sword. ²² Cast your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you; he will never let the righteous be shaken. ²³ But you, O God, will bring them down to the pit of destruction — bloodthirsty and deceitful people will not live out half their days. But I will trust in you.

¹ Be gracious to me, O God, for people are hounding me — they press against me and fight me all day long. ² My enemies pursue me all day long; many are attacking me, O Most High. ³ When I am afraid, I put my trust in you. ⁴ In God, whose word I praise — in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can mere flesh do to me? ⁵ Every day they twist what I say; all their thoughts are bent on hurting me.

⁶ They huddle together, they lurk in the shadows, watching my every step, waiting to take my life. ⁷ Can they escape by their wrongdoing? In your anger, bring the nations down, O God. ⁸ You have kept count of all my wandering; collect my tears in your bottle — are they not recorded in your book? ⁹ When I cry out to you, then my enemies will turn back — this I know, for God is on my side. ¹⁰ In God, whose word I praise — in the LORD, whose word I praise.

¹¹ In God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can anyone do to me? ¹² I am bound by the vows I made to you, O God; I will offer you my thanks. ¹³ For you have delivered my life from death — and surely my feet from stumbling — so that I may walk before God in the light of life.

¹ Be gracious to me, O God, be gracious — for in you my soul takes refuge; in the shadow of your wings I will shelter until this storm passes. ² I cry to God Most High, to God who fulfills his purpose for me. ³ He will send from heaven and save me, rebuking those who trample me. Selah. God will send his steadfast love and his faithfulness. ⁴ My life is surrounded by lions; I lie down among those who are hungry for blood — people whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords. ⁵ Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; let your glory cover all the earth.

⁶ They set a net for my feet — I was brought low. They dug a pit in my path — but they have fallen into it themselves. Selah. ⁷ My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast! I will sing and make music. ⁸ Awake, my soul! Awake, harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn. ⁹ I will give thanks to you, Lord, among the peoples; I will sing praises to you among the nations. ¹⁰ For your steadfast love reaches to the heavens, your faithfulness to the skies.
¹¹ Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; let your glory be over all the earth.

¹ Do you rulers truly speak what is right? Do you judge people fairly? ² No — in your heart you devise injustice, and your hands inflict violence on the earth. ³ The wicked go astray from birth; from the moment they are born, liars wander off the path. ⁴ Their venom is like the venom of a snake, like a deaf cobra that stops up its ears, ⁵ unwilling to hear the voice of a charmer, no matter how skillful the spell.

⁶ Break the teeth in their mouths, O God; shatter the fangs of the lions, LORD. ⁷ Let them vanish like water that seeps away; let them wither like trampled grass. ⁸ Let them be like a slug that melts as it moves, like a stillborn child that never sees the sun. ⁹ Before your pots can feel the heat of the thornwood — whether green or ablaze — he will sweep them away. ¹⁰ The righteous will be glad when they witness his vengeance; they will bathe their feet in the blood of the wicked.
¹¹ And people will say, "Surely there is a reward for the righteous; surely there is a God who judges the earth."

¹ Rescue me from my enemies, O my God; protect me from those who rise up against me. ² Deliver me from those who work evil, and save me from violent men. ³ See how they lie in wait for my life; fierce men conspire against me — for no fault of mine, O LORD. ⁴ They stir themselves up with no wrongdoing on my part; rouse yourself to help me and see! ⁵ You, LORD God of hosts, God of Israel — awake to punish all the nations; show no mercy to those who wickedly betray. Selah.

⁶ Each evening they return, howling like dogs and prowling the city. ⁷ Watch them spew with their mouths — swords are on their lips — "Who is listening?" they say. ⁸ But you, LORD, laugh at them; you scoff at all the nations. ⁹ O my Strength, I watch for you; for you, O God, are my fortress. ¹⁰ My God in his steadfast love will meet me; God will let me look in triumph on my enemies.

¹¹ Do not kill them, lest my people forget; scatter them by your power and bring them down, O Lord our shield. ¹² For the sins of their mouths, the words of their lips, let them be caught in their pride. For the curses and lies they speak, ¹³ consume them in your wrath; consume them until they are no more. Let them know that God rules over Jacob to the ends of the earth. Selah. ¹⁴ Each evening let them return, howling like dogs and prowling the city. ¹⁵ Let them roam about in search of food, and growl if they do not find enough.

¹⁶ But I will sing of your strength; I will shout aloud your steadfast love in the morning. For you have been my fortress and my refuge in the day of my distress. ¹⁷ O my Strength, to you I sing praises; for you, O God, are my fortress, the God who shows me steadfast love.

¹ O God, you have rejected and broken us; you have been angry — now restore us! ² You shook the land and split it open; repair its cracks, for it is falling apart. ³ You have shown your people desperate times; you have made us drink wine that staggers us. ⁴ But you have raised a banner for those who fear you — a rallying point away from the archers. Selah. ⁵ Deliver those you love; save us and answer us by your right hand.

⁶ God has spoken in his holiness: "With joy I will divide up Shechem and measure out the Valley of Sukkoth. ⁷ Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is my helmet, Judah is my scepter. ⁸ Moab is my washbasin; on Edom I toss my sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph." ⁹ Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom? ¹⁰ Is it not you, O God, who rejected us? Will you not march out with our armies?
¹¹ Give us help against the enemy, for human help is worthless. ¹² With God we will do mighty things; it is he who will crush our enemies.

¹ Hear my cry, O God; listen to my prayer. ² From the ends of the earth I call to you, when my heart grows faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I. ³ For you have been my refuge, a strong tower against the enemy. ⁴ Let me dwell in your tent forever; let me take refuge under the shelter of your wings. Selah. ⁵ For you, O God, have heard my vows; you have given me the inheritance of those who fear your name.

⁶ Extend the years of the king's life; may his years span many generations. ⁷ May he be enthroned before God forever; appoint your steadfast love and faithfulness to preserve him. ⁸ Then I will ever sing praises to your name, as I fulfill my vows day after day.

¹ My soul rests in God alone; my salvation comes from him. ² He alone is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I will never be greatly shaken. ³ How long will you all attack someone — would you batter them down, this leaning wall, this tottering fence? ⁴ They only plan to bring him down from his height; they love deception. With their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah. ⁵ Rest in God alone, my soul; my hope comes from him.

⁶ He alone is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I will not be shaken. ⁷ My salvation and my honor rest in God; my mighty rock, my refuge is God. ⁸ Trust in him at all times, you people; pour out your hearts to him — God is our refuge. Selah. ⁹ Surely people of low estate are nothing; people of high estate are a lie. Placed on the scales, they weigh less than a breath. ¹⁰ Don't trust in extortion or put false hope in stolen goods; even if your wealth grows, don't set your heart on it.
¹¹ God has spoken once; twice I have heard this: that power belongs to God, ¹² and that to you, O Lord, belongs steadfast love — for you repay everyone according to what they have done.

¹ O God, you are my God; I seek you eagerly. My soul thirsts for you; my flesh longs for you in a dry and weary land with no water. ² I have looked for you in the sanctuary, longing to see your power and glory. ³ Because your steadfast love is better than life itself, my lips will praise you. ⁴ So I will bless you as long as I live; in your name I will lift up my hands. ⁵ My soul will be satisfied as with the richest of foods; with joyful lips my mouth will praise you,

⁶ when I remember you on my bed and meditate on you through the watches of the night. ⁷ Because you have been my help, I sing in the shadow of your wings. ⁸ My soul clings to you; your right hand holds me close. ⁹ But those who seek to destroy my life will go down to the depths of the earth. ¹⁰ They will fall by the sword and become food for jackals.
¹¹ But the king will rejoice in God; all who swear by him will glory in him, while the mouths of liars will be silenced.

¹ Hear my voice, O God, in my complaint; protect my life from the threat of the enemy. ² Hide me from the conspiracy of the wicked, from the scheming of wrongdoers, ³ who sharpen their tongues like swords and aim bitter words like arrows, ⁴ shooting from ambush at the blameless — suddenly, without fear. ⁵ They encourage one another in evil plans; they talk about hiding their snares and say, "Who will see them?"

⁶ They plot injustice and say, "We have perfected a shrewd scheme." The human heart and mind are deep. ⁷ But God will shoot them with his arrow; suddenly they will be wounded. ⁸ He will turn their own tongues against them, and all who see them will shake their heads. ⁹ All people will fear and proclaim what God has done, pondering what he has carried out. ¹⁰ The righteous will rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in him; all the upright in heart will glory.

¹ Praise awaits you, O God, in Zion; to you vows will be fulfilled. ² O you who hear prayer, to you all flesh will come. ³ When we are overwhelmed by our sins, you forgive our transgressions. ⁴ Blessed is the one you choose and bring near to dwell in your courts! We shall be satisfied with the goodness of your house, the holiness of your temple. ⁵ With awesome deeds you answer us in righteousness, O God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas,

⁶ the one who by his strength set the mountains in place, girded with power, ⁷ who stills the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, the uproar of the nations. ⁸ The inhabitants of the ends of the earth stand in awe at your signs. You make the gateways of morning and evening to shout for joy. ⁹ You visit the earth and water it; you greatly enrich it — the river of God is full of water. You provide the people with grain, for so you have prepared it. ¹⁰ You water its furrows abundantly, settling its ridges, softening it with showers, blessing its growth.

¹¹ You crown the year with your goodness, and your paths overflow with abundance. ¹² The pastures of the wilderness overflow; the hills are wrapped in joy. ¹³ The meadows are clothed with flocks; the valleys are decked with grain — they shout for joy, they sing.

¹ Shout for joy to God, all the earth; ² sing the glory of his name; make his praise glorious. ³ Say to God, "How awesome are your deeds! So great is your power that your enemies cringe before you. ⁴ All the earth worships you and sings to you; they sing praises to your name." Selah. ⁵ Come and see what God has done — his awesome deeds on behalf of humanity.

⁶ He turned the sea into dry land; they passed through the river on foot — there we rejoiced in him. ⁷ He rules by his power forever; his eyes keep watch over the nations — let not the rebellious rise up against him. Selah. ⁸ Bless our God, you peoples; let the sound of his praise be heard. ⁹ He has kept us among the living and has not let our feet slip. ¹⁰ For you, O God, have tested us; you have refined us like silver.

¹¹ You brought us into the net; you laid heavy burdens on our backs. ¹² You let others ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water — but you brought us out to a place of abundance. ¹³ I will come into your house with burnt offerings; I will fulfill my vows to you, ¹⁴ the vows my lips uttered and my mouth spoke when I was in trouble. ¹⁵ I will offer you burnt offerings of fattened animals, with the sweet smoke of rams; I will offer bulls and goats. Selah.

¹⁶ Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell what he has done for my soul. ¹⁷ I cried out to him with my mouth, and praise was on my tongue. ¹⁸ If I had cherished sin in my heart, the Lord would not have listened. ¹⁹ But God has indeed listened; he has heard the voice of my prayer. ²⁰ Blessed be God, who has not rejected my prayer or removed his steadfast love from me!

¹ May God be gracious to us and bless us and make his face shine on us — Selah — ² so that your ways may be known on earth, your salvation among all nations. ³ Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you. ⁴ Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for you judge the peoples with fairness and guide the nations of the earth. Selah. ⁵ Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you.
⁶ The earth has yielded its harvest; God, our own God, will bless us. ⁷ God will bless us, and all the ends of the earth will fear him.

¹ Let God rise up; let his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee before him. ² As smoke is blown away, so drive them away; as wax melts before a flame, so let the wicked perish before God. ³ But let the righteous be glad; let them rejoice before God; let them celebrate with joy. ⁴ Sing to God, sing praises to his name; lift up a song to him who rides through the deserts — his name is the LORD — and exult before him. ⁵ Father of the fatherless and defender of widows is God in his holy dwelling.

⁶ God sets the lonely in families; he leads out the prisoners with singing; but the rebellious live in a sun-scorched land. ⁷ O God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through the wilderness, Selah, ⁸ the earth shook, the heavens poured down rain before God — Sinai itself trembled before God, the God of Israel. ⁹ You shed abundant rain, O God; you restored your inheritance when it was parched. ¹⁰ Your flock settled in it; in your goodness, O God, you provided for the needy.

¹¹ The Lord gave the word; great was the company of those who carried the news. ¹² "Kings and their armies are fleeing, fleeing" — and women at home are dividing the plunder. ¹³ Even while you sleep among the sheepfolds, the wings of a dove are covered with silver, its feathers shimmering gold. ¹⁴ When the Almighty scattered kings there, snow fell on Zalmon. ¹⁵ The mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; a mountain with many peaks is the mountain of Bashan.

¹⁶ Why do you look with envy, you many-peaked mountains, at the mountain God chose for his dwelling? For the LORD will dwell there forever. ¹⁷ The chariots of God are tens of thousands, thousands upon thousands; the Lord has come from Sinai into his holy place. ¹⁸ When you ascended on high, you led a host of captives; you received gifts from people — even from the rebellious — so that the LORD God might dwell there. ¹⁹ Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burdens, the God who is our salvation. Selah. ²⁰ Our God is a God who saves; the LORD our God holds the keys of escape from death.

²¹ Surely God will shatter the heads of his enemies, the hairy crown of those who walk in their guilty ways. ²² The Lord said, "I will bring them back from Bashan, I will bring them back from the depths of the sea, ²³ so that you may plunge your feet in blood, so that the tongues of your dogs may have their share of your enemies." ²⁴ Your procession has come into view, O God — the procession of my God and King into the sanctuary. ²⁵ The singers in front, the musicians last, between them the young women playing tambourines.

²⁶ Bless God in the great congregation; bless the LORD, O you who are of Israel's fountain. ²⁷ There is little Benjamin in the lead, the princes of Judah in their company, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali. ²⁸ Summon your power, O God; show us your strength, O God, as you have done for us before. ²⁹ Because of your temple at Jerusalem, kings will bring gifts to you. ³⁰ Rebuke the beasts among the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples, until they bow down with bars of silver. Scatter the nations who delight in war.

³¹ Nobles will come from Egypt; Ethiopia will stretch out her hands to God. ³² Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth; sing praises to the Lord, Selah, ³³ to him who rides through the ancient highest heavens — he thunders with a mighty voice. ³⁴ Ascribe power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, whose power is above the clouds. ³⁵ Awesome is God from his sanctuary — the God of Israel; he gives power and strength to his people. Blessed be God!

¹ Save me, O God, for the waters have come up to my neck. ² I sink in deep mud where there is no foothold; I have come into the deep waters, and the flood sweeps over me. ³ I am weary with my crying; my throat is dry. My eyes grow dim with waiting for my God. ⁴ Those who hate me without cause outnumber the hairs of my head; many are my enemies without reason — those who seek to destroy me. I am forced to restore what I did not steal. ⁵ O God, you know my foolishness; my guilt is not hidden from you.

⁶ Let not those who hope in you be put to shame through me, O Lord GOD of hosts; let not those who seek you be brought to disgrace through me, O God of Israel. ⁷ For it is for your sake that I have borne reproach; shame has covered my face. ⁸ I have become a stranger to my brothers, an outsider to my mother's children. ⁹ Zeal for your house has consumed me; the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me. ¹⁰ When I wept and fasted, it turned to my reproach.

¹¹ When I put on sackcloth, I became a byword to them. ¹² Those who sit at the gate mock me, and the drunkards make up songs about me. ¹³ But I pray to you, O LORD, at an acceptable time. O God, in the abundance of your steadfast love, answer me in your saving faithfulness. ¹⁴ Deliver me from sinking in the mire; let me be rescued from my enemies and from the deep waters. ¹⁵ Let not the flood sweep over me, or the deep swallow me, or the pit close its mouth over me.

¹⁶ Answer me, O LORD, for your steadfast love is good; according to your abundant mercy, turn to me. ¹⁷ Do not hide your face from your servant — I am in distress; answer me quickly. ¹⁸ Draw near to me; redeem me; ransom me because of my enemies. ¹⁹ You know my reproach, my shame, and my dishonor; all my enemies are before you. ²⁰ Reproach has broken my heart, and I am in despair. I looked for sympathy, but there was none — for comforters, but I found no one.

²¹ They gave me poison for food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. ²² Let their own table become a snare for them, and when they are at peace, let it be a trap. ²³ Let their eyes grow dark so they cannot see, and make their bodies shake continually. ²⁴ Pour out your indignation on them; let your burning anger overtake them. ²⁵ May their camp be left desolate; may no one dwell in their tents.

²⁶ For they persecute those you have struck down; they heap on the pain of those you have wounded. ²⁷ Charge them with guilt upon guilt; do not let them share in your righteousness. ²⁸ Let them be blotted out of the book of life and not be listed with the righteous. ²⁹ But I am afflicted and in pain; let your salvation, O God, set me on high. ³⁰ I will praise the name of God with a song; I will magnify him with thanksgiving.

³¹ This will please the LORD more than an ox or a bull with horns and hoofs. ³² When the humble see this, they will be glad; you who seek God, let your hearts revive. ³³ For the LORD hears the needy and does not despise his own who are captives. ³⁴ Let heaven and earth praise him, the seas and everything that moves in them. ³⁵ For God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah; his people will settle there and possess it.
³⁶ The children of his servants will inherit it, and those who love his name will dwell in it.

¹ Come quickly to help me, O God; LORD, hurry to my rescue. ² Let those who seek my life be ashamed and confused; let those who want to hurt me be turned back in disgrace. ³ Let those who say "Aha! Aha!" be turned back in shame. ⁴ Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you; let those who love your salvation say continually, "Let God be magnified!" ⁵ But I am poor and needy — come quickly to me, O God. You are my help and my deliverer; O LORD, do not delay.

¹ In you, O LORD, I have taken refuge; never let me be put to shame. ² In your righteousness, rescue me and deliver me; turn your ear to me and save me. ³ Be my rock of refuge, to which I can always come; give the command to save me, for you are my rock and my fortress. ⁴ Rescue me, O my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the cruel and unjust. ⁵ For you are my hope, O Lord GOD; you are my confidence from my youth.

⁶ You have upheld me from birth; you drew me from my mother's womb. My praise is always of you. ⁷ I have been like a wonder to many, but you are my strong refuge. ⁸ My mouth is filled with your praise and with your glory all day long. ⁹ Do not cast me away in the time of old age; do not forsake me when my strength is spent. ¹⁰ For my enemies are talking about me; those who watch to take my life take counsel together,

¹¹ saying, "God has forsaken him; pursue and seize him, for there is no one to rescue him." ¹² O God, do not be far from me; O my God, come quickly to help me. ¹³ Let those who accuse me be put to shame and consumed; let those who seek to harm me be covered with scorn and disgrace. ¹⁴ But I will hope continually and will praise you yet more and more. ¹⁵ My mouth will tell of your righteous acts and of your deeds of salvation all the day, for I cannot count them all.

¹⁶ I will come with the mighty deeds of the Lord GOD; I will proclaim your righteousness — yours alone. ¹⁷ O God, from my youth you have taught me, and I still proclaim your wondrous works. ¹⁸ So even to old age and gray hair, O God, do not forsake me, until I proclaim your might to another generation, your power to all those to come. ¹⁹ Your righteousness, O God, reaches the high heavens. You who have done great things — O God, who is like you? ²⁰ You who have made me see many troubles and calamities will revive me again; you will bring me up again from the depths of the earth.

²¹ You will increase my greatness and comfort me again. ²² I will also praise you with the harp for your faithfulness, O my God; I will sing praises to you with the lyre, O Holy One of Israel. ²³ My lips will shout for joy when I sing praises to you; my soul, which you have redeemed. ²⁴ And my tongue will speak of your righteousness all day long, for those who wanted to harm me have been brought to shame and disgrace.

¹ O God, give the king your justice, and your righteousness to the king's son. ² May he judge your people with righteousness, and your poor with justice. ³ Let the mountains bring prosperity to the people, the hills the fruit of righteousness. ⁴ May he defend the cause of the poor among the people, deliver the children of the needy, and crush the oppressor. ⁵ May he endure as long as the sun, as long as the moon, throughout all generations.

⁶ May he be like rain that falls on a freshly cut field, like showers that water the earth. ⁷ In his days let the righteous flourish, and abundance of peace, until the moon is no more. ⁸ May he rule from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth. ⁹ May those who live in the desert bow before him; may his enemies lick the dust. ¹⁰ May the kings of Tarshish and the coastal lands bring tribute; may the kings of Sheba and Seba present gifts.

¹¹ Yes, let all kings bow down to him; let all nations serve him. ¹² For he will deliver the needy who cry out, the afflicted who have no one to help. ¹³ He will take pity on the weak and the needy and save the lives of the needy. ¹⁴ He will rescue them from oppression and violence, for their lives are precious in his sight. ¹⁵ Long may he live; may gold from Sheba be given to him. May people ever pray for him and bless him all day long.

¹⁶ May grain abound throughout the land; on the tops of the hills may it sway. May the crops flourish like Lebanon, and the people thrive like grass of the field. ¹⁷ May his name endure forever; may it continue as long as the sun. Then all nations will be blessed through him, and they will call him blessed. ¹⁸ Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous things. ¹⁹ Blessed be his glorious name forever; may the whole earth be filled with his glory. Amen and Amen. ²⁰ This concludes the prayers of David son of Jesse.

¹ Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart. ² But as for me, my feet had almost slipped; I had nearly lost my footing. ³ For I was envious of the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked. ⁴ For they have no pain in their death; their bodies are fat and sleek. ⁵ They have no trouble like other people; they are not plagued like everyone else.

⁶ Therefore pride is their necklace; violence covers them like a garment. ⁷ Their eyes swell with luxury; their hearts overflow with fantasies. ⁸ They scoff and speak with malice; with arrogance they threaten oppression. ⁹ They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut through the earth. ¹⁰ Therefore his people turn to them and drink up waters in abundance.

¹¹ And they say, "How would God know? Does the Most High know anything?" ¹² Look at these wicked people — always at ease, they keep getting richer. ¹³ Surely in vain I have kept my heart clean and washed my hands in innocence. ¹⁴ All day long I have been afflicted; every morning brings more punishment. ¹⁵ If I had said, "I will speak like them," I would have betrayed your children.

¹⁶ When I tried to understand all this, it was too hard for me — ¹⁷ until I entered the sanctuary of God; then I understood their final destiny. ¹⁸ Surely you place them on slippery ground; you cast them down to ruin. ¹⁹ How suddenly they are destroyed, completely swept away by terrors! ²⁰ Like a dream when you wake up — so when you arise, Lord, you despise them as fantasies.

²¹ When my heart was embittered, and I was pricked with pain in my soul, ²² I was senseless and ignorant; I was like an animal before you. ²³ Yet I am always with you; you hold me by my right hand. ²⁴ You guide me with your counsel, and afterward you will receive me to glory. ²⁵ Whom do I have in heaven but you? And on earth I desire nothing but you.

²⁶ My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever. ²⁷ For those who are far from you will perish; you destroy all who are unfaithful to you. ²⁸ But as for me, drawing near to God is my good. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may tell of all your works.

¹ O God, why have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smolder against the sheep of your pasture? ² Remember the people you purchased long ago, the tribe you redeemed as your own inheritance — this Mount Zion, where you have dwelt. ³ Turn your steps toward these utter ruins, all this destruction the enemy has done to the sanctuary. ⁴ Your enemies have roared inside your holy meeting place; they set up their banners as signs of conquest. ⁵ They seemed like people raising axes to cut down a forest of trees.

⁶ And now they smash all the carved woodwork with hatchets and hammers. ⁷ They have burned down your sanctuary to the ground; they have defiled the dwelling place of your name. ⁸ They said to themselves, "We will crush them altogether." They have burned every place where God was worshiped in the land. ⁹ We see no signs from God; no prophets remain, and none of us knows how long this will last. ¹⁰ How long, O God, will our enemies mock? Will the enemy revile your name forever?

¹¹ Why do you hold back your hand — your right hand? Take it from the folds of your garment and destroy them! ¹² Yet God is my King from of old, working salvation throughout the earth. ¹³ You divided the sea by your might; you broke the heads of the monsters in the waters. ¹⁴ You crushed the heads of Leviathan; you gave him as food for the creatures of the desert. ¹⁵ You split open springs and streams; you dried up rivers that never run dry.

¹⁶ The day is yours, and the night is yours too; you established the moon and the sun. ¹⁷ You set all the boundaries of the earth; you made summer and winter. ¹⁸ Remember, LORD, how the enemy has mocked you, how a foolish people have scorned your name. ¹⁹ Do not hand over the life of your dove to wild beasts; do not forget the lives of your afflicted people forever. ²⁰ Have regard for your covenant, for the dark places of the earth are full of the haunts of violence.

²¹ Let not the oppressed turn away in shame; let the poor and needy praise your name. ²² Rise up, O God, and defend your cause; remember how fools mock you all day long. ²³ Do not forget the clamor of your adversaries, the uproar of your enemies, which rises continually.

¹ We give thanks to you, O God; we give thanks, for your name is near. People tell of your wonderful deeds. ² "I choose the appointed time; it is I who judge with equity. ³ When the earth and all its people quake, it is I who hold its pillars firm. ⁶ At your rebuke, O God of Jacob, both horse and chariot lie still. ⁷ It is you alone who are to be feared. ¹¹ Make your vows to the LORD your God and keep them; let all who are around him bring gifts to the one to be feared. ¹² He breaks the spirit of rulers; he is feared by the kings of the earth.
